one_liner: GitHub offers a broad, free, self-serve REST and GraphQL API with OAuth apps, GitHub Apps and PATs, plus an official GitHub-maintained MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth apps support the authorization code flow and device flow. Personal access tokens are static bearer tokens. GitHub Apps use a JWT you mint yourself to get installation tokens. Basic auth with a password has been retired, and the Basic auth text in the evidence is from an old Enterprise 11.10 doc.
access_notes: A free GitHub account gives working tokens, and the API is not billed separately. Authenticated requests are limited to 5,000 per hour.
blocker_notes: No blocker. Some individual endpoints depend on the paid plan of the underlying feature.

evidence.quote: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` in a GitHub Actions workflow.
GitHub's OAuth implementation supports the standard [authorization code grant type](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.1) and the OAuth 2.0 [Device Authorization Grant]
Generate a JSON Web Token (JWT) for your app.
The REST API is included with GitHub accounts; GitHub plans start at Free ($0/month), Team ($4/user/month), and Enterprise (from $21/user/month), but the API is not billed separately.
All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
The GraphQL API does not support any queries or mutations that require you to authenticate with a JWT.
Many REST API endpoints require authentication or return additional information if you are authenticated.
The GitHub MCP server is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provided and maintained by GitHub.
